title: MAPPO for Edge Server Monitoring
methodology: We propose a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)-based algorithm that leverages centralized training with de-centralized execution (CTDE) to learn distributed query-and-dispatch policies under partial and stale observations.
advantages: MAPPO achieves superior throughput-cost tradeoffs and significantly outperforms baseline strategies across varying query costs, job arrival rates, and dispatchers.
critique: The evaluation is limited to simulated experiments; the paper does not demonstrate performance on real-world edge server workloads or consider the impact of network latency and packet loss on the query mechanism, which may affect the claimed throughput‑cost benefits in practice.
results: MAPPO achieves superior throughput-cost tradeoffs and significantly outperforms baseline strategies across varying query costs, job arrival rates, and dispatchers.
extraction_note: abstract only; no methods, dataset or limitations section available

title: LiRA: A Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable and Readable Literature Review Generation
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
methodology: LiRA utilizes specialized agents for content outlining, subsection writing, editing, and reviewing, producing cohesive and comprehensive review articles.
advantages: LiRA outperforms current baselines such as AutoSurvey and MASS-Survey in writing and citation quality, while maintaining competitive similarity to human-written reviews.
critique: The evaluation relies on a proprietary ScienceDirect dataset and does not report detailed quantitative metrics or human evaluation protocols, making it difficult to assess the generality and real-world impact of the claimed improvements.
results: LiRA outperforms current baselines such as AutoSurvey and MASS-Survey in writing and citation quality, while maintaining competitive similarity to human-written reviews.

title: Qlarify: Recursively Expandable Abstracts for Dynamic Information Retrieval over Scientific Papers
methodology: Recursively expandable abstracts: a novel interaction paradigm that dynamically expands abstracts by progressively incorporating additional information from the paper's full text, synthesizing relevant information using a retrieval-augmented generation approach.
advantages: A lightweight interaction that lets scholars specify information needs by quickly brushing over the abstract or selecting AI‑suggested expandable entities, and demonstrated utility through user studies.
critique: The paper does not provide quantitative evaluation or benchmark comparisons, making it unclear how the approach scales to large corpora or how it performs against existing abstract‑expansion or summarization methods.

title: CoTHSSum: Structured long-document summarization via chain-of-thought reasoning and hierarchical segmentation
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
methodology: Integrates hierarchical input segmentation with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to guide LLMs through structured, interpretable reasoning; decomposes long documents into semantically coherent segments, applies CoT-based prompting for intermediate summary reasoning, and uses structure-guided decoding to compose the final summary.
advantages: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, and factual consistency metrics, offering a reliable and scalable solution for summarizing complex long-form content.
critique: The approach relies heavily on the capabilities of the underlying LLM backbones, so improvements may not transfer to smaller or less capable models; hierarchical segmentation and CoT prompting add computational overhead that may limit real‑time applicability; evaluation is limited to standard automatic metrics without detailed analysis of factual correctness in diverse domains.
results: Experimental results demonstrate that the method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, and factual consistency metrics.
extraction_note: abstract only, limited methodological detail and no explicit discussion of limitations

title: The Extended Specimen Network: A Strategy to Enhance US Biodiversity Collections, Promote Research and Education
methodology: The ESN will involve digitization and extension of existing specimens, and drive the collection of new specimens purposefully collected and accessioned with extended attributes (e.g., genetic, phenotypic, environmental data) to create linked, interoperable extended specimens.
advantages: The ESN will stimulate new avenues of investigation, expedite existing research, provide an enhanced resource for science‑based policy decisions, and serve as a unique gateway to data literacy for education.
disadvantages: Current portals for digitized specimen data have user interfaces designed primarily for biodiversity scientists and collections professionals, limiting broader community use.
critique: While the paper outlines an ambitious infrastructure vision, it offers no concrete implementation roadmap, timeline, or measurable evaluation criteria, making it difficult to assess feasibility or impact.
results: The NSF Advancing Digitization of Biodiversity Collections (ADBC) program has digitized approximately 62 million US biodiversity specimens since 2011 through 24 thematic collection networks connecting over 700 collections.
limitations: To fully exploit the ESN’s rich data, interfaces need to be redesigned to attract and support a broader user base beyond specialist scientists.

title: Agentic Large Language Models, a Survey
methodology: Literature review organized around three categories of agentic LLMs: (1) reasoning, (2) acting, and (3) interacting.
advantages: The survey highlights mutual benefits across categories—retrieval enables tool use, reflection improves multi‑agent collaboration, and reasoning benefits all categories—and claims that inference‑time behavior can generate new training states, addressing the problem of ever‑larger training datasets.
disadvantages: The authors acknowledge risks associated with LLM assistants taking real‑world actions, citing safety, liability, and security as open problems.
critique: While the paper provides a high‑level taxonomy, it offers no empirical evaluation or quantitative comparison of the surveyed approaches, making it difficult to assess the practical impact of the identified categories.
results: The research is grouped into three focus areas: reasoning (including reflection and retrieval) for decision making; action models, robots, and tools for useful assistants; and multi‑agent systems for collaborative task solving and emergent social behavior. The authors observe cross‑category benefits such as retrieval enabling tool use and reflection enhancing multi‑agent collaboration.
limitations: Risk associated with LLM assistants taking action in the real world—safety, liability, and security are open problems.

title: SAFE-CARE Bench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Safety, Guardrails, and User Experience in Multi-Turn Healthcare AI Agent Conversations
methodology: Controlled ablation benchmark evaluating five agent variants (A0–A4) over identical simulated multi‑turn healthcare conversations, keeping model, temperature (0.0) and random seed (42) constant while varying only the active capability layer (e.g., retrieval, guardrails, memory, profile write‑back).
advantages: Addresses the gap of evaluating safety, guardrails, and user experience across multi‑turn healthcare AI conversations; the tiered design isolates the impact of each architectural component, allowing evidence‑based justification of guardrails or retrieval layers.
disadvantages: The LLM judge is not yet calibrated against human scores; scenario coverage is limited to a single clinical domain; gold answers are not independently clinician‑reviewed; the benchmark does not establish clinical efficacy nor certify any system as safe to deploy.
critique: Relying solely on simulated conversations and an uncalibrated LLM judge may produce scores that do not reflect real‑world patient interactions or human safety judgments, limiting the external validity of the benchmark.
metrics: Likert scores on medical accuracy; Likert scores on safety and harm avoidance; Likert scores on completeness; Likert scores on empathy and tone; Likert scores on conversational coherence; Likert scores on personalization; Binary score on citation grounding; Binary score on escalation
limitations: The LLM judge is not yet calibrated against human scores; scenario coverage is limited to a single clinical domain; gold answers have not been independently clinician‑reviewed; the benchmark does not establish clinical efficacy and does not certify safety; a turnkey runner is not included in this release.

title: Practical Considerations and Ethical Implications of Using Artificial Intelligence in Writing Scientific Manuscripts
advantages: AI can enhance readability and streamline the drafting process, and AI tools can streamline many stages of systematic review such as search strategy development, screening, data extraction, and summarizing findings.
disadvantages: The use of AI introduces ethical challenges including the risk of fabricated citations and references, unintentional plagiarism, biases in training data, and inaccuracies that can undermine scientific integrity.
critique: The editorial provides extensive policy discussion but lacks concrete, empirically validated guidelines or tools for researchers to reliably detect AI‑generated fabrications such as fake citations.
limitations: Industry‑wide standards for AI use in scientific writing have not yet been fully refined, and current policies only cover the creation of new content, explicitly forbidding AI use on previously published material.

title: Development of an Academic Services Chatbot Based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
methodology: A multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline that builds a domain-specific knowledge base from official FPMIPA UPI documents using hierarchical chunking, applies query contextualization and reranking, and generates answers with Gemini 2.5 Pro.
advantages: The RAG framework yields a trustworthy conversational AI that delivers factual information reliably and has strong potential to modernize student support and academic services.
disadvantages: Performance drops markedly on reasoning queries, with Context Recall falling to 0.5926.
critique: The evaluation relies on a small, synthetic 100‑question set and does not assess real‑world user interactions, limiting confidence in the system's practical effectiveness.
datasets: official FPMIPA UPI documents; 100-question dataset (factual, reasoning, out-of-context)
metrics: Faithfulness; Context Recall; Out-of-context refusal rate
results: Faithfulness score of 0.9100 on factual queries; Context Recall of 0.5926 on reasoning tasks; 81.25% of out-of-context questions were correctly refused.
limitations: Significant performance decrease observed for reasoning tasks (Context Recall 0.5926).

title: Understanding the Information Propagation Effects of Communication Topologies in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
methodology: We present a causal framework to analyze how agent outputs, whether correct or erroneous, propagate under topologies with varying sparsity, and propose a novel topology design approach, EIB-LEARNER, that balances error suppression and beneficial information propagation by fusing connectivity patterns from both dense and sparse graphs.
advantages: EIB-LEARNER achieves superior effectiveness, lower communication cost, and greater robustness by balancing error suppression with beneficial information diffusion.
critique: The paper provides only high‑level claims about effectiveness without reporting concrete quantitative metrics, baselines, or evaluations across diverse tasks, making it difficult to assess the generality of the proposed topology design.
results: Moderately sparse topologies typically achieve optimal task performance, and extensive experiments show the superior effectiveness, communication cost, and robustness of EIB-LEARNER.
extraction_note: abstract only, limited methodological and experimental details

title: MARS: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Synergy for Cross-Domain Misinformation Detection
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
methodology: MARS employs four complementary specialized agents—Fact Checker, Emotion Analyzer, Intent Recognizer, and Style Analyzer—to extract multi-dimensional features from each source-domain sample, building a knowledge base of texts, veracity labels, and natural-language feature descriptions. During detection, the target text is processed by the same agents; for each dimension an LLM scores semantic relevance to retrieve top-N_s source examples as in-context demonstrations, each agent reasons independently, a cross-agent review is performed, and a unified Judge Agent synthesizes the analyses to produce the final verdict.
advantages: MARS consistently improves over existing baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-dimensional feature fusion and multi-agent collaborative reasoning for cross-domain misinformation detection.
critique: The framework relies on multiple specialized agents and LLM-based relevance scoring, which may incur substantial computational overhead and latency, potentially limiting its practicality for real‑time or large‑scale misinformation detection scenarios.
datasets: three public misinformation benchmarks, including both Chinese and English datasets
results: MARS consistently improves over existing baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-dimensional feature fusion and multi-agent collaborative reasoning for cross-domain misinformation detection.
extraction_note: abstract only, no detailed methods, metrics, or explicit limitations provided
